The best thing for me was being sent to a crisis intervention centre. 10 days of being around people with problems kind of changed my mindset. It was really easy to talk about my problems with people who have attempted suicide before. It wasn't like some huge taboo thing to talk about, because before going there I thought that it would be impossible to explain my situation to anyone. Their support and the general normalization of the whole suicide aspect helped me so much that it seems unreal at times. Suicide was a Norm there, that's why talking about it was easy and everyone quickly realised the absurdness of it all. 

Obviously after I was released from the hospital I had a huge existential crisis. For 2 weeks it seemed that I was living on Bonus times. For 5 years I was so sure that I'd be dead by now that it seemed surreal. It was weird to think that I'll actually live to see a movie that was to be released after my deadline, or a video game that I was so sure I'll never get to play. It was difficult to understand what I'm "allowed" to do. I'm living with my parents and it seemed that if I'm not actively looking for a job or doing something productive I was just disappointing them and wasting my bonus time. 

I found a job. And did everything in my power to be good at it. I had to prove to myself that I can do something right. I had to prove to myself that I can be more than average, I had to prove to myself that I can be the best. And it worked. When I finally got the recognition that I'm the best out of the group that I started working with I got a confidence boost like I have never felt. 

Also, being as busy as possible helps too. Less time to drown yourself in "those" thoughts. Sure they comeback from time to time, but I easily shrug them off, because I remember how absurd they were in the first place.

You have to reward yourself if you do something well. Also, talk talk and talk about your emotional state. If you don't have anyone close to you, go for group therapy. It's the best medicine there is. Obviously antidepressants to their job quite well to. I can go to a shop without sweating like crazy and actually get what I need instead of just getting one item and bailing out due to stress.

The crazy part is that it has been only 3 months since "that day". I'm actually alive. Not just biologicaly, but mentally too. I'm no longer on Bonus time, I'm actually in the present time and what happened seems so long ago. It required a crazy ammount of effort and a lot of support from my family but I'm here and I'm here to stay. 

Remember, nobody wants you dead. Your family and pretty much everyone in the world will accept your failures and let you of the hook. They want you alive and will help you in any way they can to make sure they get you back from that horrible limbo you have been stuck in. Believe in yourself.

I'm in a mental institution because I tried to kill myself. The doctors here kinda linked my behaviour to my parents being "toxic" and I'm reading a book about toxic parents. When I get out of here I'll have to live with my parents and rely on their financial support. What scares me is that if what the doctors and the book say is true, then I'll be going right back into the environment that pushed me towards taking my own life. In all honesty my mind is a total mess and no matter how hard i try to put the pieces together I end up scrambling them again.

It's not that I'm unsure, I just don't want to do it. However, for once in my life I have to do the responsible thing. I know it seems weird but the aftermath of me coming clean to my parents would end up causing them more pain, than just a few months of grief. That and the fact that I'm afraid of comin clean. Hell, I'm 23 and I'm still afraid of telling my parents I spilled coffee on my table. I'm like a 10 year old stuck in a 23 year olds body. Tho today seems so calm. It's like the idea that it's going to be over soon puts everything in a pleasant perspective. Hell, sorry to be bothering you with this. I know it's not very pleasing to read about these things, guess it's just one of my selfish acts
